Subject: Follow-up: Atlas Health deployment & data isolation preferences

Hi Elena / Marcus —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap of decisions and open items so we have alignment before the security deep dive: 

1) Current leaning: Atlas wants strong tenant isolation and cryptographic separation for PHI-like records. Team asked whether Dedicated capacity would satisfy that or if Private (VPC/on-prem) is required.
2) Redwood short answers: Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools and tenant-level encryption at rest; Private VPC gives customer-managed networking, stricter egress control, and can be packaged for on-prem if required.
3) Open items for your security team: network egress restrictions, KMS/HSM requirements, data retention policies, and whether Atlas needs physical separation (on-prem) vs virtual isolation (dedicated with encryption & strict tenancy).

Attachments: I attached the Atlas Data Isolation spreadsheet you mentioned for your internal reference (Atlas_Data_Isolation_Reqs.xlsx).

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with our SRE and your security contacts (please share preferred times).
- I'll also drop a short one-pager showing the difference in controls between Dedicated and Private VPC and a matrix that maps each control to the deployment option.

If useful I can propose a tentative timeline: discovery next week, followed by a security questionnaire turn-around within 5 business days.

Best,

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the recap and the spreadsheet. A few clarifying questions from our Security & Infrastructure teams before we schedule the deep dive: 

- Encryption: Is customer-managed KMS supported in Dedicated, or is that only available in Private? Our policy requires customer-managed keys for production PHI workloads.
- Network isolation: Can Dedicated be configured with a customer-managed VPC peering (no public internet egress) or is that only possible with Redwood Private?
- Auditability: We need immutable audit logs with at least 1 year retention and syslog export. Are these provided in Dedicated or do we need Private to get the exports wired to our SIEM?
- SLA & tenancy: For latency-sensitive inference, we prefer dedicated GPU capacity; would purchasing Dedicated guarantee single-tenant GPU pools for our model instances or are there shared resources?

Also attached is a short requirements sheet we started (Atlas_Data_Isolation_Reqs.xlsx) — happy to fill more detailed answers after your responses.

Main ask: please confirm which controls are available in Dedicated vs Private and whether there are configuration-dependent caveats. If possible, send the redwood_dedicated_security_matrix.xlsx or a one-pager.

Thanks —
Elena Rossi
VP, Infrastructure & Security
Atlas Health

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@atlashealth.com>, Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 15:40:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Atlas Health deployment & data isolation preferences

Elena —

Thanks, great questions. Short answers up front, then proposed follow-ups: 

- KMS: Customer-managed KMS is supported in Private by default. For Dedicated, we can enable customer-key wraps in many cases (bring-your-own-KMS) but it depends on the Commitment tier and region; we'll confirm the supported KMS providers for your region in the SRE call.

- Network isolation: Dedicated can be configured with private networking and peering (no public egress) in many deployments — we call this "Dedicated with VPC Peering". Private VPC gives you the additional option of a customer-controlled control plane and more restrictive routing (e.g., proxy only to approved destinations).

- Auditability & logs: Dedicated provides audit logs and export hooks; for guaranteed immutable exports to your SIEM and extra-retention policies we typically recommend Private (we can also offer log-forwarding from Dedicated as a managed addon).

- Tenancy & GPUs: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity (no noisy neighbor on the same reserved hosts for your committed pool). The runtime still uses shared control plane components in hosted mode; if you need physical separation of the entire stack we can discuss Private on-prem.

I've attached a brief matrix that maps these controls (redwood_dedicated_security_matrix.xlsx) and a one-pager on the Private VPC option (redwood_private_vpc_onepager.pdf). See attached.

Proposed next steps:
1) Security deep-dive: SRE + Solutions Engineer (Lauren) + Atlas Security (please include the lead who owns KMS). Suggested slots: Wed 14 Jan 09:00-11:00 PT or Thu 15 Jan 14:00-16:00 PT.
2) I'll share our SOC2 report under NDA and a draft of the KMS configuration guide right after the call.
3) If Atlas is leaning Dedicated, we can prepare a dedicated capacity estimate and an addendum for BYOK/KMS within 3 business days after the SRE call.

If you prefer, we can run a short pilot on Dedicated with a limited dataset while you validate log exports and KMS behavior.

Best,
Vivek

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_security_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB); redwood_private_vpc_onepager.pdf (pdf, 85KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: AtlasHealth - recommended proposal path

Team — quick internal note to capture next steps before the SRE call with Atlas: 

Summary: Atlas is primarily concerned with cryptographic control (BYOK) and network egress controls for PHI workloads. They also prefer guaranteed reserved GPUs for latency. They are undecided between Dedicated (with BYOK & VPC peering) and Private (customer-managed control plane).

Recommendation:
- Lead with Dedicated + BYOK + VPC peering as the least-friction commercial option. Emphasize pilot to validate log forwarding and KMS behavior.
- Prepare a fallback offering: Private (VPC with optional on-prem) if Atlas legal requires full control of the control plane or requires immutable on-site logs.
- Pre-gather SOC2 + KMS provider compatibility and a sample addendum for BYOK.

Action items:
- Vivek: schedule SRE call with proposed times and confirm Atlas security lead.
- Karthik: prepare the BYOK compat matrix for GCP/AWS regions (due EOD before call).
- Lauren: pull SOC2 + sample log-forwarding config and drop into the HubSpot deal record.

I'll be on the call; suggest we keep the first call focused on requirements and avoid pricing until we confirm controls.

— Lauren
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
